title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is p. 750 of the continuation of La Longue Marche (1981). The previous page sets up a profinite group M with a map M -> G(A_Q), where G is an algebraic group over Q and X_G is a Shimura-type datum. Hypotheses 1°–4° are stated there, together with a 'germ of discretification' pi_0 and a subgroup G_0 of elements commensurating pi_0. Grothendieck calls this a 'dictionary', and a margin note says G_0 plays the role of a discrete Galois or Teichmüller group.

On this page he reformulates the axiomatics ('Réflexion faite...'). The data are:
(1) M, a profinite 'LT-group'.
(2) A normal closed subgroup Pi of M carrying an 'L-structure'. This seems to be some linear-algebraic or adelic structure, e.g. roughly Pi ≈ the profinite completion of SL(2,Z). The L-structure on Pi is what defines the LT-structure on M.
(3) A 'discretification' Pi_0 of Pi: a discrete group, dense in Pi, compatible with the L-structure, so that Pi is the closure of Pi_0.
(4) A discrete group 𝔊_0 ⊃ Pi_0 normalizing Pi_0, mapping to M, whose closure 𝔊^ in M is normal in M. The special case 𝔊_0 = Pi_0 is allowed.

This gives diagram (32):
- profinite row: Pi ⊂ 𝔊^ ⊂ M, with tau = 𝔊^/Pi, Gamma = M/𝔊^, N = M/Pi;
- discrete row: Pi_0 ⊂ 𝔊_0 with tau_0 = 𝔊_0/Pi_0;
- vertical maps: dense inclusions Pi_0 -> Pi and 𝔊_0 -> 𝔊^.

He remarks that 𝔊^ is a quotient of the profinite completion of 𝔊_0. He does not (yet) require it to be the full completion, which is a congruence-subgroup-type issue.

The next page gives the interpretation:
- tau_0 is a discrete Teichmüller group and tau its completion;
- Gamma = M/𝔊^ is a profinite Galois group.

Two extreme cases follow:
(a) 𝔊_0 = Pi_0. This is the arithmetic fundamental group of a smooth relative stack (multiplicité) of finite type over a field finitely generated over Q: Pi is the geometric pi_1 and Gamma the Galois group.
(b) 𝔊_0/Pi_0 is (of finite index in) the Teichmüller group of Pi_0. This is the 'modular' situation, e.g. the universal curve over M_{g,n}, or M_{1,1} with Pi = SL2(Z)^.

The purpose is to axiomatize the 'Galois–Teichmüller' situation. Profinite arithmetic fundamental groups, with their discrete topological skeleta and their Galois quotients, are meant to be compared with adelic groups G(A_Q) attached to Shimura-type data.
errors: Arrows '1 <- Pi' / '1 <- Pi_0' are written backwards. Read them as 1 -> Pi_0 -> 𝔊_0, i.e. inclusions; the '1 <-' on the top row is crossed out anyway.

Implicit assumptions are not stated on this page: Pi_0 -> Pi is injective with dense image; 𝔊_0 -> M is a homomorphism (possibly not injective); 𝔊_0 ∩ Pi = Pi_0 or a commensurability condition. These are left vague.

Example Pi ≈ SL(2,Z)^: since SL(2,Z) lacks the congruence subgroup property, its full profinite completion does not embed in SL2(Ẑ). An 'L-structure' that is genuinely linear/adelic would see only the congruence completion. This tension is presumably why he writes 'à peu près' and declines to require 𝔊^ to be the full completion.

ideas.what: Axiomatic triple: profinite M, normal 'geometric' subgroup Pi, Galois quotient M/𝔊^, with discrete skeleta Pi_0 ⊂ 𝔊_0 and quotients tau_0 (discrete Teichmüller) -> tau (profinite Teichmüller) -> Gamma (Galois)
ideas.modern_name: Arithmetic fundamental group exact sequences of moduli stacks; Galois–Teichmüller theory (outer Galois action on Teichmüller tower)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse 1984), Ihara, Deligne, Drinfeld, Nakamura, Schneps–Lochak
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme and La Longue Marche treat the Teichmüller tower and the Galois action; this specific axiomatization with diagram (32) appears unpublished

ideas.what: 'Discretification' of a profinite group with extra structure: a dense discrete subgroup Pi_0 whose closure is Pi; closure of 𝔊_0 is a quotient of its profinite completion
ideas.modern_name: Discrete dense lattices in profinite groups; congruence vs profinite completion (congruence subgroup problem); profinite rigidity
ideas.usually_credited_to: Serre, Bass–Milnor–Serre (congruence); Grothendieck 1970 (profinite completion of discrete groups)
ideas.where_published: Related in spirit to 'Représentations linéaires et compactification profinie des groupes discrets' (1970); the term 'discrétification' here appears unpublished

ideas.what: Linking profinite Galois–Teichmüller data to adelic groups G(A_Q) and Shimura-type data (X_G) as a 'dictionary'
ideas.modern_name: Fundamental groups of Shimura varieties / modular curves and adelic Galois representations
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara, Deligne, Shimura; later anabelian work on Shimura varieties

missed.claim: Grothendieck outlines an axiomatic 'dictionary' between (i) profinite groups M with a linear/adelic structure (L/LT-structures), discretifications and Galois quotients and (ii) moduli stacks / Shimura-type data (G, X_G) over Q. This is an attempted characterization of which profinite extension data come from geometry (smooth stacks, or the modular/Teichmüller situation). It was not developed in published form.
missed.quote: un sous-groupe discret 𝔊_0 ⊃ Π_0 normalisant Π_0 ... tel que son adh. 𝔊^_0 dans M soit distingué dans M
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It anticipates a unifying formalism for the anabelian Galois–Teichmüller setting and fundamental groups of Shimura varieties. Such a formalism is still largely absent: the literature treats these cases separately, and congruence-completion versus full-completion issues are handled ad hoc.

missed.claim: The page makes explicit the role of the congruence/profinite completion gap. 𝔊^ is only a quotient of the profinite completion of 𝔊_0, with SL2(Z)^ given as a model. This ties the congruence subgroup problem for mapping class groups and SL2(Z) to his Galois–Teichmüller programme.
missed.quote: 𝔊 s'identifie à un quotient du complété profini de 𝔊_0, mais ne s'exige pas pour le moment qu'il soit isomorphe
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: The congruence subgroup problem for mapping class groups (Asada, Boggi and others) is now known to be tied to the profinite Teichmüller tower. This page shows Grothendieck framing it inside an adelic dictionary, a link that may be undercredited.

deep.surprise_reason: This is an unpublished axiomatic framework connecting Galois–Teichmüller profinite groups with adelic Shimura-type data and 'discretifications'. That is notable as intent, but it is sketchy and the individual ingredients are known later themes.
transcription_corrections: Margin insertion 'son adh.' (with caret) belongs before 𝔊^_0. The line reads: 'tel que son adh. 𝔊^_0 = adh. de 𝔊_0 dans M soit distingué dans M'.
In the diagram, the brace N spans the whole top row Pi ... M (N = M/Pi). tau is over Pi -> 𝔊^ and Gamma over 𝔊^ -> M; tau_0 is under Pi_0 -> 𝔊_0.
The middle profinite group is written 𝔊^ (with a mark), with '= 𝔊^_0' beneath it; the Pi column has '= Pi^_0' beneath.
'(NB. au cas particulier [-important-] où 𝔊_0 = Π_0)': the crossed-out word is plausibly 'important'.
Next-page 'idem pour Γ et Γ_0' should probably read tau and tau_0, since the discrete Teichmüller group is tau_0 = 𝔊_0/Pi_0.
